jobs.name: turn
jobs.prompt: Locked-off static side-view camera, pure black background. The mechanical lion from the first frame turns around on the spot to face the opposite direction. A heavy big-cat pivot in place: its weight settles back onto the hind legs, the head and shoulders swing round toward the camera, the forepaws lift and re-plant one after the other as the forequarters come round through a front three-quarter view, the hindquarters step round after them, and the tail swings last as a counterbalance. It finishes standing still in exactly the mirrored pose of the last frame. It never walks away from its spot, never changes size, and stays centred in frame with all four paws on the same ground line. Same ivory armour plates, same violet joint lights and eyes, same mane, no redesign. No camera movement, no zoom, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no dust, no sparks, no glow effects, no text.

jobs.name: idle
jobs.prompt: Locked-off static side-view camera, pure black background. The mechanical lion from the first frame stands watching, alert and alive, without moving from its spot: its ribcage rises and falls with two slow heavy breaths, the head lifts a little and settles, the jaw loosens and closes, the mane plates flex, and the tail sways slowly from side to side as a counterweight. All four paws stay planted exactly where they are for the whole shot — no step, no walk, no turn. It ends in exactly the same pose it started in, so the shot loops. Same size, same position, same ivory armour plates, same violet joint lights and eyes. No camera movement, no zoom, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no dust, no sparks, no glow effects, no text.

jobs.name: roar
jobs.why: the 2026-10-04 roar was filmed over a lit floor and haze; its cut-out lost chunks of the mane and legs and could not be re-keyed. This one is on clean black, from the same standing frame as the turn and the idle.
jobs.prompt: Locked-off static side-view camera, pure black background. The mechanical lion from the first frame roars without leaving its spot. First second: it inhales — the chest swells, the head draws back and lifts, the shoulders rise, the jaw still closed. Then it ROARS: the head thrusts forward and up, the jaw opens very wide showing metal teeth, the mane plates flare outward, the whole body braces into it and trembles, held for a second and a half. Then the jaw closes, the head lowers, and it settles back into exactly the standing pose of the first frame. All four paws stay planted where they are the whole time — no step, no walk, no turn, no rearing onto the hind legs. Same size, same position, same ivory armour plates, same violet joint lights and eyes, no redesign. Nothing comes out of the mouth: no breath, no beam, no shockwave, no glow effects, no sparks, no dust. No camera movement, no zoom, no ground plane, no floor, no cast shadow, no spotlight, no haze, no text.
